AGRICULTURE — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #9
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: AGRICULTURE
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Why does a lid on a pot save fuel? (1 mark)
   A. It keeps the heat in so food cooks faster
   B. It stops the food from cooking
   C. It makes the pot lighter
   D. It cools the food

2. What do roots of a fruit tree do? (1 mark)
   A. Hold the tree and take in water and food
   B. Collect sunlight
   C. Make fruits
   D. Produce seeds

3. How should the seedling be removed from its polythene bag? (1 mark)
   A. By pulling the stem hard
   B. Carefully so the ball of soil around roots does not break
   C. By throwing it
   D. By cutting the roots

4. Which of these fruits does best in cool highland areas? (1 mark)
   A. Coconut
   B. Tree tomato
   C. Cashew nut
   D. Mango

5. What is irrigation? (1 mark)
   A. Digging the soil
   B. Spraying crops with medicine
   C. Giving water to crops by ways other than rain
   D. Harvesting crops

6. Which pupil is saving water? (1 mark)
   A. One who waters with a drip bottle beside each plant
   B. One who waters at midday
   C. One who leaves the tap running
   D. One who pours buckets over the whole bed

7. What should be placed under a tippy tap? (1 mark)
   A. A radio
   B. A bed
   C. A basin or a soak pit
   D. A plant only

8. Which refuse can be put in the compost heap? (1 mark)
   A. Batteries
   B. Vegetable peelings
   C. Tins
   D. Plastic bottles

9. What should you wear when handling rubbish? (1 mark)
   A. Nothing
   B. Only a hat
   C. Gloves
   D. Sandals only

10. Which food is usually boiled? (1 mark)
   A. Potatoes
   B. Bhajia
   C. Chips
   D. Mandazi

11. Which method uses water and a mop? (1 mark)
   A. Sweeping
   B. Burning
   C. Dusting
   D. Mopping

12. Why should a container seedbed have holes at the bottom? (1 mark)
   A. To make it lighter
   B. Extra water can drain out
   C. Seeds can escape
   D. Insects can leave

13. Why is a cloth placed over the opening of the water container? (1 mark)
   A. To make the container heavier
   B. To keep dirt from blocking the small holes
   C. To make the water hot
   D. To colour the water

14. Which of these is a green material for a compost heap? (1 mark)
   A. Dry leaves
   B. Straw
   C. Dry maize stalks
   D. Fresh cut grass

15. Which of these can happen if a child eats only ugali? (1 mark)
   A. Growing very tall at once
   B. Never feeling tired
   C. Getting all vitamins
   D. Feeling weak and getting sick often

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
16. Explain the difference between domestic and wild animals. (2 marks)

17. Explain pruning. (2 marks)

18. Compare even tacking and long and short tacking. Say which is quicker and which holds more firmly. (4 marks)

19. A drip system drips very fast at one hole and not at all at another. Explain what may be wrong and how to fix each. (4 marks)

20. State three dangers of using fuels at home and how to avoid one of them. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
AGRICULTURE — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #9 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — It keeps the heat in so food cooks faster
   Less heat escapes so less fuel is used.

2. A — Hold the tree and take in water and food
   Roots anchor and absorb.

3. B — Carefully so the ball of soil around roots does not break
   Broken roots harm the seedling.

4. B — Tree tomato
   Tree tomato grows well in cooler highlands, while coconut, cashew and mango like warm places.

5. C — Giving water to crops by ways other than rain
   Irrigation means supplying water to crops artificially.

6. A — One who waters with a drip bottle beside each plant
   Drip watering is the most water-saving.

7. C — A basin or a soak pit
   To catch the dirty water.

8. B — Vegetable peelings
   Organic waste rots.

9. C — Gloves
   Gloves protect from germs and cuts.

10. A — Potatoes
   Potatoes are commonly boiled.

11. D — Mopping
   Mopping washes floors.

12. B — Extra water can drain out
   Waterlogged soil rots seeds and roots.

13. B — To keep dirt from blocking the small holes
   Dirt would clog the tiny holes.

14. D — Fresh cut grass
   Green materials are fresh and wet, such as fresh grass, peelings and fresh dung.

15. D — Feeling weak and getting sick often
   One food cannot supply all nutrients.

SECTION B
----
16. (2 marks)
   Answer: Domestic animals are kept and cared for by people. Wild animals live freely in nature.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct description.

17. (2 marks)
   Answer: It is cutting off dead, weak or crossing branches so that light and air can reach the plant.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for cutting, 1 mark for the purpose.

18. (4 marks)
   Answer: Even tacking is more even and holds more firmly; long and short tacking is quicker because each stitch covers more cloth.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for each stitch description, 1 each for quicker and firmer.

19. (4 marks)
   Answer: The first hole is too big, so tie cloth around it or use a smaller hole. The other hole is blocked, so clear it gently with a thin wire.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for cause and fix for both holes.

20. (3 marks)
   Answer: Fire burns, charcoal fumes are poisonous and gas can leak. Avoid one by keeping children away from fire, cooking in a place with fresh air or closing the gas valve after use.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for dangers, 1 mark for a correct way to avoid one.
